intent: Make the first production-critical Helm terminal harnesses incapable of contacting the operator's default tmux server by routing boot, PTY, alternate-screen, and Terminal Guardian calls through one Bash 3.2-compatible CODEX_MANAGED_PURPOSE_PID private-socket helper while preserving exact 80x24 proof and bounded cleanup.

negative_controls.name: bare-default-tmux-regression-is-detected
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import pathlib,subprocess,sys; p=pathlib.Path('terminal/scripts/boot_smoke.sh'); t=p.read_text(); old='codex_managed_tmux new-session'; t.count(old) == 1 or sys.exit(3); p.write_text(t.replace(old,'tmux new-session',1)); sys.exit(subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','-q','tests/test_terminal_tmux_isolation.py','-k','target_harnesses_use_only_managed_calls']).returncode)"

interface_mismatches: boot_smoke.sh and pty_smoke.sh currently issue bare tmux commands, so a test can create, inspect, send keys to, or kill a session on the operator's default server.

alternate_screen_check.sh and terminal_guardian_preflight.sh already use private servers, but their independent naming and cleanup logic do not enforce the shared CODEX_MANAGED_PURPOSE_PID ownership boundary.
The compact proof contract requires an exact 80x24 pane on a private server with no inherited tmux configuration, not merely a uniquely named session on an unspecified server.
honest_blockers: This packet migrates four production-critical harnesses only. The explicitly forbidden truecolor, golden-capture, trace, assistant-event, offline-queue, slash-feedback, and model-pool harnesses require later packets and must not be described as isolated by this result.
The helper proves test-process ownership of a private tmux server; it does not authorize touching, renaming, attaching to, or stopping the operator's live or durable tmux sessions.
Passing an isolated 80x24 harness is proof of terminal geometry and cleanup, not proof of seven-seat OnCall liveness, route readiness, performance, packaging, or production cutover.
session_entry.rollback: Revert this packet commit to restore the prior harness-local tmux calls. The packet creates no durable tmux sessions and migrates no operator state; each managed server is PID-qualified and stopped by its owning harness.
